title.zh: 卷三十五 列傳第十六 高祖十二王
title.en: Volume 35 Biographies 16: Gao Zu's Twelve Princes
title.raw: 卷三十五 列傳第十六 高祖十二王 Volume 35 Biographies 16: Gao Zu's Twelve Princes

sentences.zh: 高帝十九男：昭皇后生武帝、豫章文獻王嶷；

translations.literal: Emperor Gao had nineteen sons: Empress Zhao bore Emperor Wu and Prince Wenxian of Yuzhang Ni;
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gao had nineteen sons: Empress Zhao bore Emperor Wu and Prince Wenxian of Yuzhang, Ni;

sentences.zh: 謝貴嬪生臨川獻王映、長沙威王晃；

translations.literal: Noble Consort Xie bore Prince Xian of Linchuan Ying and Prince Wei of Changsha Huang;
translations.idiomatic: Noble Consort Xie bore Prince Xian of Linchuan, Ying, and Prince Wei of Changsha, Huang;

sentences.zh: 羅太妃生武陵昭王曄；

translations.literal: Consort Dowager Luo bore Prince Zhao of Wuling Ye;
translations.idiomatic: Consort Dowager Luo bore Prince Zhao of Wuling, Ye;

sentences.zh: 任太妃生安成恭王暠；

translations.literal: Consort Dowager Ren bore Prince Gong of Ancheng Gao;
translations.idiomatic: Consort Dowager Ren bore Prince Gong of Ancheng, Gao;

sentences.zh: 陸修儀生鄱陽王鏘、晉熙王 銶；

translations.literal: Lady of Cultivated Rites Lu bore Prince of Poyang Qiang and Prince of Jinxi Qiu;
translations.idiomatic: Lady of Cultivated Rites Lu bore the Prince of Poyang, Qiang, and the Prince of Jinxi, Qiu;

sentences.zh: 袁修容生桂陽王鑠；

translations.literal: Lady of Cultivated Appearance Yuan bore Prince of Guiyang Shuo;
translations.idiomatic: Lady of Cultivated Appearance Yuan bore the Prince of Guiyang, Shuo;

sentences.zh: 何太妃生始興簡王鑒、宜都王鏗；

translations.literal: Consort Dowager He bore Prince Jian of Shixing Jian and Prince of Yidu Keng;
translations.idiomatic: Consort Dowager He bore Prince Jian of Shixing, Jian, and the Prince of Yidu, Keng;

sentences.zh: 區貴人生衡陽王鈞；

translations.literal: Lady of the District Qu bore Prince of Hengyang Jun;
translations.idiomatic: Lady of the District Qu bore the Prince of Hengyang, Jun;

sentences.zh: 張淑妃生江夏王鋒、河東王鉉；

translations.literal: Imperial Beauty Zhang bore Prince of Jiangxia Feng and Prince of Hedong Xuan;
translations.idiomatic: Imperial Beauty Zhang bore the Prince of Jiangxia, Feng, and the Prince of Hedong, Xuan;

sentences.zh: 李美人生南平王銳；

translations.literal: Lady of Beauty Li bore Prince of Nanping Rui;
translations.idiomatic: Lady of Beauty Li bore the Prince of Nanping, Rui;

sentences.zh: 第九、第十三、第十四、第 十七皇子早亡。

translations.literal: The ninth, thirteenth, fourteenth, and seventeenth princes died young.
translations.idiomatic: The ninth, thirteenth, fourteenth, and seventeenth princes died in childhood.

sentences.zh: 衡陽王鈞出繼元王后。

translations.literal: Prince of Hengyang Jun was adopted out to succeed the Prince of Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Hengyang, Jun, was given in adoption to succeed the Prince of Yuan.

sentences.zh: 臨川獻王映，字宣光，太祖第三子也。

translations.literal: Prince Xian of Linchuan Ying, styled Xuangguang, was the founding emperor's third son.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Xian of Linchuan, Ying, styled Xuangguang, was the founding emperor's third son.

sentences.zh: 宋元徽四年，解褐著作佐郎，遷撫軍行參軍，南陽王文學。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Yuanhui of Song he left coarse cloth as editorial aide, was promoted to staff officer on the Pacification Army, and literary aide to the Prince of Nanyang.
translations.idiomatic: In Song's fourth year of Yuanhui he left coarse cloth as editorial aide, then became staff officer on the Pacification Army and literary aide to the Prince of Nanyang.

sentences.zh: 沈攸之事難，太祖時領南徐州，以映為寧朔將軍，鎮京口。

translations.literal: When Shen Youzhi's troubles arose, the founding emperor then held Southern Xuzhou and made Ying General of Pacifying the North, garrisoning Jingkou.
translations.idiomatic: When Shen Youzhi rebelled, the founding emperor was holding Southern Xuzhou and appointed Ying General of Pacifying the North to garrison Jingkou.

sentences.zh: 事寧，除中軍諮議、從事中郎、輔國將軍、淮南宣城二郡太守，並不拜。

translations.literal: When the affair was settled, he was made adviser to the central army, attendant gentleman, aide to the state, general of assisting the state, and grand administrator of Huainan and Xuancheng — both posts he declined.
translations.idiomatic: After peace he was named adviser to the central army, attendant gentleman, aide to the state, and general of assisting the state, with grand administrations of Huainan and Xuancheng — all declined.

sentences.zh: 仍為假節、督南兗兗徐青冀五州諸軍事、行南兗州刺史，將軍如故。

translations.literal: He was then made acting commissioner with credentials, commander of military affairs in five provinces — Southern Yan, Yan, Xu, Qing, and Ji — and acting governor of Southern Yan, general as before.
translations.idiomatic: He was then made acting commissioner with credentials, commander of military affairs in Yan, Southern Yan, Xu, Qing, and Ji, and acting governor of Southern Yan, with rank unchanged.

sentences.zh: 尋除給事黃門侍郎，領前軍將軍，仍復為冠軍將軍、南兗州刺史，假節督，復為監軍，督五州如故。

translations.literal: Soon he was made attendant gentleman at the yellow gate, head of the vanguard army, then again champion general and governor of Southern Yan with acting credentials and command as before, and again army supervisor over the five provinces.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was attendant at the yellow gate and head of the vanguard army, then again champion general and governor of Southern Yan with credentials and command unchanged, again supervising the five provinces.

sentences.zh: 齊台建，宋帝詔封映及弟晃、曄、暠、鏘、鑠、鑒併為開國縣公，各千五百戶，未及定土宇，而太祖踐阼。

translations.literal: When the Qi regime was established, the Song emperor edicted that Ying and his brothers Huang, Ye, Gao, Qiang, Shuo, and Jian be enfeoffed as founding-county dukes, each with 1,500 households; before domains were fixed the founding emperor took the throne.
translations.idiomatic: When the Qi regime was formed, the Song emperor enfeoffed Ying and his brothers Huang, Ye, Gao, Qiang, Shuo, and Jian as founding-county dukes of 1,500 households each; before their domains were fixed the founding emperor ascended.

sentences.zh: 以映為使持節、都督荊湘雍益梁寧南北秦八州諸 軍事、平西將軍、荊州刺史。

translations.literal: Ying was made bearer of credentials, commander of military affairs in eight provinces — Jing, Xiang, Yong, Yi, Liang, Ning, and northern and southern Qin — and General Who Pacifies the West, governor of Jing.
translations.idiomatic: Ying was made bearer of credentials, commander of eight provinces — Jing, Xiang, Yong, Yi, Liang, Ning, and northern and southern Qin — and General Who Pacifies the West, with Jing as his province.

sentences.zh: 封臨川王，食邑例二千戶。

translations.literal: He was enfeoffed Prince of Linchuan with a fief of the usual two thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: He was enfeoffed as Prince of Linchuan with the usual fief of two thousand households.

sentences.zh: 又領湘州刺史。

translations.literal: He also held the governorship of Xiang.
translations.idiomatic: He also held Xiang as his province.

sentences.zh: 豫章王嶷既留鎮陝西，映亦不行。

translations.literal: Prince of Yuzhang Ni having remained to garrison western Shaanxi, Ying likewise did not go out.
translations.idiomatic: As Prince of Yuzhang Ni stayed to garrison western Shaanxi, Ying too did not take up his post.

sentences.zh: 改授散騎常侍、都督揚南徐二州諸軍事、前將軍、揚 州刺史，持節如故。

translations.literal: He was reassigned attendant at leisure, commander of military affairs in Yang and Southern Xu, former general, and governor of Yang, credentials as before.
translations.idiomatic: He was reassigned attendant at leisure, commander of Yang and Southern Xu, former general, and governor of Yang, with credentials unchanged.

sentences.zh: 國家初創，映以年少臨神州，吏治聰敏，府州曹局皆重足以奉禁令，自宋彭城王義康以後未之有也。

translations.literal: In the state's first founding, Ying at a young age held the sacred commandery; his official craft was keen, and every bureau of the princedom and prefecture walked on tiptoe to obey orders — since Song's Prince of Pengcheng Yikang there had been nothing like it.
translations.idiomatic: When the dynasty was new, Ying in his youth held the imperial metropolis; his governance was sharp, and every office of princedom and prefecture stood in awe of his orders — not since Song's Prince of Pengcheng Yikang had there been the like.

sentences.zh: 出為都督荊湘雍益梁巴寧南北秦九州諸軍事、鎮西將軍、荊州刺史，持節、常侍如故。

translations.literal: He went out as commander of military affairs in nine provinces — Jing, Xiang, Yong, Yi, Liang, Ba, Ning, and northern and southern Qin — General Who Guards the West and governor of Jing, credentials and attendant rank as before.
translations.idiomatic: He went out as commander of nine provinces — Jing, Xiang, Yong, Yi, Liang, Ba, Ning, and northern and southern Qin — General Who Guards the West and governor of Jing, with credentials and attendant rank unchanged.

sentences.zh: 給鼓吹一部。

translations.literal: He was given one set of martial pipes and drums.
translations.idiomatic: He was granted martial pipes and drums.

sentences.zh: 以國憂解散騎常侍，進號征西。

translations.literal: Because of national mourning he was relieved of attendant at leisure and advanced to General Who Pacifies the West.
translations.idiomatic: During national mourning he relinquished attendant at leisure and was advanced to General Who Pacifies the West.

sentences.zh: 永明元年入為侍中，驃 騎將軍。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongming he entered court as attendant and Rapid Cavalry General.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongming year one he entered court as attendant and Rapid Cavalry General.

sentences.zh: 二年，給油絡車。

translations.literal: In year two he was given an oiled carriage canopy.
translations.idiomatic: In year two he received an oiled carriage canopy.

sentences.zh: 五年，即本號開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: In year five he was made Grand Mentor with the same title at his present rank.
translations.idiomatic: In year five he was made Grand Mentor with ceremony equal to the Three Dukes at his present rank.

sentences.zh: 七年，薨。

translations.literal: In year seven he died.
translations.idiomatic: In year seven he died.

sentences.zh: 映善騎射，解聲律，工左右書左右射，應接賓客，風韻韶美，朝野莫不惋惜 焉。

translations.literal: Ying was skilled at mounted archery, understood music and pitch, was adept at both styles of calligraphy and both-handed shooting, received guests with grace, and his bearing was elegant — court and commoners alike mourned him.
translations.idiomatic: Ying excelled at mounted archery, understood music, mastered both calligraphic styles and ambidextrous archery, and received guests with graceful charm — all who knew him grieved.

sentences.zh: 時年三十二。

translations.literal: He was then thirty-two.
translations.idiomatic: He was thirty-two.

sentences.zh: 詔賜東園秘器，朝服一具，衣一襲。

translations.literal: An edict granted eastern-garden secret rites vessels, one set of court dress, and one suit of garments.
translations.idiomatic: An edict granted eastern-garden funeral regalia, one court robe, and one suit of garments.

sentences.zh: 贈司空。

translations.literal: He was posthumously made Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 九子皆封侯。

translations.literal: All nine sons were enfeoffed as marquises.
translations.idiomatic: All nine sons were enfeoffed as marquises.

sentences.zh: 長子子晉，歷東陽、吳興二郡太守，秘書監，領后軍將軍。

translations.literal: The eldest son Zijin served as grand administrator of Dongyang and Wuxing, director of the secretariat, and head of the rear army.
translations.idiomatic: The eldest son Zijin served as governor of Dongyang and Wuxing, director of the secretariat, and head of the rear army.

sentences.zh: 永元初，為侍中， 遷左民尚書。

translations.literal: At the start of Yongyuan he was attendant, then promoted minister of the left for the people.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Yongyuan he was attendant, then promoted to minister of the left for the people.

sentences.zh: 坐從妹祖日不拜，為有司所奏，事留中，子晉遂不復拜。

translations.literal: He was impeached for not bowing on his cousin's ancestral day; the matter was held at court and Zijin thereafter never bowed again.
translations.idiomatic: He was impeached for failing to bow on his cousin's ancestral memorial day; the matter lingered at court, and Zijin never bowed again.

sentences.zh: 梁王定京邑，猶服侍中服。

translations.literal: When the Liang prince secured the capital he still wore attendant's dress.
translations.idiomatic: When the Liang prince secured the capital he still wore court attendant's robes.

sentences.zh: 入梁為輔國將軍、高平太守。

translations.literal: Under Liang he was made general of assisting the state and grand administrator of Gaoping.
translations.idiomatic: Under Liang he was made general of assisting the state and governor of Gaoping.

sentences.zh: 第二子子游，州陵侯。

translations.literal: The second son Ziyou was Marquis of Zhouling.
translations.idiomatic: The second son Ziyou was Marquis of Zhouling.

sentences.zh: 解褐員外 郎，太子洗馬，歷琅邪、晉陵二郡太守，黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: He left coarse cloth as outside gentleman, crown prince's chamberlain, and served as grand administrator of Langye and Jinling and attendant at the yellow gate.
translations.idiomatic: He left coarse cloth as outside gentleman and crown prince's chamberlain, then governed Langye and Jinling and served as attendant at the yellow gate.

sentences.zh: 好音樂，解絲竹雜藝。

translations.literal: He loved music and understood string and wind arts.
translations.idiomatic: He loved music and mastered string and wind instruments.

sentences.zh: 梁初坐閨門淫穢及殺人，為有司所奏，請議禁錮。

translations.literal: Early in Liang he was impeached for licentious conduct within the inner quarters and murder; the authorities requested he be confined.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Liang he was impeached for debauchery within the inner quarters and murder; the authorities asked that he be confined.

sentences.zh: 子晉謀反，兄弟並伏誅。

translations.literal: When Zijin plotted rebellion, the brothers were all executed.
translations.idiomatic: When Zijin rebelled, the brothers were all executed.

sentences.zh: 長沙威王晃，字宣明，太祖第四子也。

translations.literal: Prince Wei of Changsha Huang, styled Xuanming, was the founding emperor's fourth son.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Wei of Changsha, Huang, styled Xuanming, was the founding emperor's fourth son.

sentences.zh: 少有武力，為太祖所愛。

translations.literal: In youth he had martial strength and was loved by the founding emperor.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he was physically powerful and a favorite of the founding emperor.

sentences.zh: 宋世解褐秘書郎邵陵王友，不拜。

translations.literal: In Song times he left coarse cloth as secretariat gentleman and friend to the Prince of Shaoling — and declined.
translations.idiomatic: Under Song he was made secretariat gentleman and friend to the Prince of Shaoling — and declined.

sentences.zh: 升明二年，代兄映為寧朔將軍、淮南宣城二郡太守。

translations.literal: In the second year of Shengming he replaced his elder brother Ying as General of Pacifying the North and grand administrator of Huainan and Xuancheng.
translations.idiomatic: In Shengming year two he replaced his elder brother Ying as General of Pacifying the North and governor of Huainan and Xuancheng.

sentences.zh: 初，沈攸之事起，晃便弓馬，多從武容，熏赫都街，時人為之語曰：「煥煥蕭四傘。

translations.literal: When Shen Youzhi's affair began, Huang was skilled at bow and horse and went with many martial attendants, dominating the capital streets; people made a saying: 「Splendid, splendid, Xiao the Fourth with his umbrella.」
translations.idiomatic: When Shen Youzhi rebelled, Huang rode out with many armed attendants and filled the capital streets; people said, 「Splendid, splendid — Xiao the Fourth and his umbrella.」

sentences.zh: 」 其年，遷為持節、監豫司二州郢州之西陽諸軍事、西中郎將、豫州刺史。

translations.literal: That year he was promoted bearer of credentials, supervisor of military affairs in Yu and Si and Xiyang in Ying, General of the West Center, and governor of Yu.
translations.idiomatic: That year he was made bearer of credentials, supervisor of Yu and Si and of Xiyang in Ying, General of the West Center, and governor of Yu.

sentences.zh: 太祖踐祚，晃欲陳政事，輒為典簽所裁，晃執殺之。

translations.literal: When the founding emperor took the throne, Huang wished to present state affairs but was always cut off by the chief clerk; Huang seized and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: When the founding emperor ascended, Huang tried to present affairs of state but the chief clerk always blocked him; Huang seized and killed the man.

sentences.zh: 上大怒，手詔賜杖。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly angered and by hand-edict granted him a beating staff.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was furious and by his own hand edicted a beating with the staff.

sentences.zh: 尋 遷使持節、都督南徐兗二州諸軍事、后將軍、南徐州刺史。

translations.literal: Soon he was moved to bearer of credentials, commander of Southern Xu and Yan, rear general, and governor of Southern Xu.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was bearer of credentials, commander of Southern Xu and Yan, rear general, and governor of Southern Xu.

sentences.zh: 世祖為皇太子，拜武進陵，于曲阿后湖斗隊，使晃御馬軍，上聞之，又不悅。

translations.literal: When the Shizu was crown prince, he paid respects at Wujin tomb; at the rear lake of Qu'a they drilled in ranks, and Huang was made to command the mounted army — the emperor heard and was again displeased.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu was crown prince he visited Wujin tomb; at Qu'a's rear lake they drilled in ranks and Huang was set to command the horse army — the emperor heard and was displeased again.

sentences.zh: 入為侍中、護軍將軍， 以國憂，解侍中，加中軍將軍。

translations.literal: He entered court as attendant and Defender General; because of national mourning he was relieved of attendant and made general of the central army.
translations.idiomatic: He entered court as attendant and Defender General; during national mourning he left the attendant post and was made general of the central army.

sentences.zh: 太祖臨崩，以晃屬世祖，處以輦轂近蕃，勿令遠出。

translations.literal: As the founding emperor lay near death he entrusted Huang to the Shizu, placing him in the capital's near domains — do not let him go far away.
translations.idiomatic: On his deathbed the founding emperor entrusted Huang to Emperor Wu, keeping him in the capital's nearby domains — never far away.

sentences.zh: 永明元年，上遷南徐州刺史竟陵王子良為南兗州，以晃為使持節、都督南徐 兗二州諸軍事、鎮軍將軍、南徐州刺史。

translations.literal: In Yongming year one the emperor moved Southern Xu governor Prince of Jingling Ziliang to Southern Yan and made Huang bearer of credentials, commander of Southern Xu and Yan, General Who Guards the Army, and governor of Southern Xu.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongming year one the emperor shifted Southern Xu governor Prince of Jingling Ziliang to Southern Yan and made Huang bearer of credentials, commander of Southern Xu and Yan, General Who Guards the Army, and governor of Southern Xu.

sentences.zh: 入為散騎常侍，中書監。

translations.literal: He entered court as attendant at leisure and director of the secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He entered court as attendant at leisure and director of the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 諸王在京都，唯置捉刀左右四十人。

translations.literal: Princes in the capital were allowed only forty blade-bearing attendants.
translations.idiomatic: Princes residing in the capital were allowed only forty blade-bearing guards.

sentences.zh: 晃愛武飾，罷徐州還，私載數百人仗還 都，為禁司所覺，投之江水。

translations.literal: Huang loved martial display; returning from Xu he secretly carried several hundred weapons back to the capital; the prohibition office discovered them and threw them into the river.
translations.idiomatic: Huang loved martial display; returning from Xu he secretly brought several hundred weapons to the capital; the prohibition office found them and cast them into the river.

sentences.zh: 世祖禁諸王畜私仗，聞之大怒，將糾以法。

translations.literal: The Shizu forbade princes to keep private arms; hearing this he was greatly angered and was about to punish by law.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu forbade princes private weapons; hearing of it he was furious and nearly prosecuted Huang by law.

sentences.zh: 豫章王嶷于御前稽首流涕曰：「晃罪誠不足宥。

translations.literal: Prince of Yuzhang Ni kowtowed before the imperial presence, weeping: 「Huang's crime truly cannot be pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Yuzhang Ni kowtowed before the throne in tears: 「Huang's crime truly cannot be forgiven.

sentences.zh: 陛下當憶先朝念白象。

translations.literal: Your Majesty should recall the late emperor's memory of White Elephant.」
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty should remember how the late emperor cherished White Elephant.」

sentences.zh: 」白象，晃小字 也。

translations.literal: White Elephant was Huang's childhood name.
translations.idiomatic: White Elephant was Huang's childhood name.

sentences.zh: 上亦垂泣。

translations.literal: The emperor also wept.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wept as well.

sentences.zh: 太祖大漸時，誡世祖曰：「宋氏若不骨肉相圖，他族豈得乘其衰弊，汝深戒之。

translations.literal: When the founding emperor was critically ill he admonished the Shizu: 「If the Song house does not plot against its own flesh, other clans cannot ride their decline — you must deeply guard against this.」
translations.idiomatic: On his deathbed the founding emperor warned Emperor Wu: 「If the Song house does not turn on its own kin, no other clan can exploit its weakness — guard against this deeply.」

sentences.zh: 」故世祖終無異意。

translations.literal: Therefore the Shizu never harbored a different intent toward him.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore Emperor Wu never truly turned against him.

sentences.zh: 然晃亦不見親寵。

translations.literal: Yet Huang was also not treated with intimate favor.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Huang was never treated with intimate favor either.

sentences.zh: 當時論者以世祖優於魏文， 減于漢明。

translations.literal: Contemporaries held the Shizu superior to Wei Wen and inferior to Han Ming.
translations.idiomatic: Contemporaries judged Emperor Wu better than Cao Pi and less than Liu Zhuang of Han Ming.

sentences.zh: 尋加晃鎮軍將軍，轉丹陽尹，常侍、將軍如故。

translations.literal: Soon Huang was made General Who Guards the Army and transferred to governor of Danyang, attendant and general as before.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was made General Who Guards the Army and governor of Danyang, with attendant rank and generalship unchanged.

sentences.zh: 又為侍中、護軍將軍，鎮軍 如故。

translations.literal: He was again attendant and Defender General, General Who Guards the Army as before.
translations.idiomatic: He was again attendant and Defender General, still General Who Guards the Army.

sentences.zh: 尋進號車騎將軍，侍中如故。

translations.literal: Soon he was advanced to General of the Chariots and Cavalry, attendant as before.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was advanced to General of the Chariots and Cavalry, attendant as before.

sentences.zh: 給油絡車，鼓吹一部。

translations.literal: He was given an oiled carriage canopy and one set of martial pipes and drums.
translations.idiomatic: He received an oiled carriage canopy and martial pipes and drums.

sentences.zh: 八年，薨，年三十一。

translations.literal: In year eight he died, aged thirty-one.
translations.idiomatic: In year eight he died at thirty-one.

sentences.zh: 賜東園秘器，朝服一具，衣一襲。

translations.literal: He was granted eastern-garden secret vessels, one court robe, and one suit.
translations.idiomatic: He was granted eastern-garden funeral regalia, one court robe, and one suit.

sentences.zh: 即本號，贈開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: At his present rank he was posthumously made Grand Mentor with ceremony equal to the Three Dukes.
translations.idiomatic: At his present rank he was posthumously made Grand Mentor with Three-Dukes ceremony.

sentences.zh: 世祖嘗幸鐘山，晃從駕，以馬槊刺道邊枯櫱，上令左右數人引之，銀纏皆卷 聚，而槊不出。

translations.literal: The Shizu once visited Zhongshan; Huang followed the carriage and with a cavalry lance pierced a withered stump by the road; the emperor had several men pull — the silver bindings all coiled up yet the lance would not come free.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu once visited Zhongshan; Huang followed and pierced a roadside dead stump with his lance; the emperor had several men pull — the silver bindings coiled but the lance would not budge.

sentences.zh: 乃令晃復馳馬拔之，應手便去。

translations.literal: He then ordered Huang to charge again and pull it; it came free at once.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered Huang to charge and pull again; it came free at once.

sentences.zh: 每遠州獻駿馬，上輒令晃于華林 中調試之。

translations.literal: Whenever distant provinces presented fine horses, the emperor always had Huang test them in the Flowery Grove.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever distant provinces sent fine horses, the emperor had Huang test them in the Flowery Grove.

sentences.zh: 太祖常曰：「此我家任城也。

translations.literal: The founding emperor often said: 「This is my family's Prince of Ren.」
translations.idiomatic: The founding emperor often said: 「This is our house's Prince of Ren.」

sentences.zh: 」世祖緣此意，故諡曰威。

translations.literal: The Shizu followed that thought, hence the posthumous name Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu followed that sentiment, hence the posthumous epithet Wei.

sentences.zh: 武陵昭王曄，字宣照，太祖第五子也。

translations.literal: Prince Zhao of Wuling Ye, styled Xuanzhao, was the founding emperor's fifth son.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Zhao of Wuling, Ye, styled Xuanzhao, was the founding emperor's fifth son.

sentences.zh: 母羅氏，從太祖在淮陰，以罪誅，曄年四歲，思慕不異成人，故每見愛。

translations.literal: His mother was the Luo clan; she followed the founding emperor at Huaiyin and was executed for a crime; Ye at four years mourned with longing no different from an adult — therefore he was always loved.
translations.idiomatic: His mother was Lady Luo; she had followed the founding emperor at Huaiyin and was executed; at four Ye grieved like a grown man — and was always cherished for it.

sentences.zh: 初除冠軍將軍，轉征虜將軍。

translations.literal: He was first made champion general, then transferred General Who Punishes the Barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: He was first champion general, then General Who Punishes the Barbarians.

sentences.zh: 曄剛穎俊出， 工弈棋，與諸王共作短句，詩學謝靈運體，以呈上，報曰：「見汝二十字，諸兒作中最為優者。

translations.literal: Ye was forceful and outstanding, skilled at chess; with the other princes he composed short verses in Xie Lingyun's manner and presented them; the reply said: 「Seeing your twenty characters — among the boys' work this is finest.
translations.idiomatic: Ye was sharp and outstanding, skilled at chess; with his brothers he wrote short verses in Xie Lingyun's style and presented them; the emperor replied: 「In your twenty characters this is the best of the boys' work.

sentences.zh: 但康樂放蕩，作體不辨有首尾，安仁、士衡深可宗尚，顏延之抑 其次也。

translations.literal: Yet Lingyun is unrestrained — his pieces have no clear head or tail; Anren and Shiheng are truly to be honored; Yan Yanzhi ranks below them.」
translations.idiomatic: Yet Lingyun is unrestrained — his pieces lack clear beginning and end; Pan Yue and Lu Ji are truly worth emulating; Yan Yanzhi ranks beneath them.」

sentences.zh: 」建元三年，出為持節、都督會稽東陽新安永嘉臨海五郡軍事、會稽太守，將軍如故。

translations.literal: In the third year of Jianyuan he went out bearer of credentials, commander of military affairs in five commanderies — Kuaiji, Dongyang, Xin'an, Yongjia, and Linhai — and governor of Kuaiji, general as before.
translations.idiomatic: In Jianyuan year three he went out bearer of credentials, commander of Kuaiji, Dongyang, Xin'an, Yongjia, and Linhai, and governor of Kuaiji, rank unchanged.

sentences.zh: 上遣儒士劉瓛往郡，為曄講《五經》。

translations.literal: The emperor sent the scholar Liu Huan to the commandery to lecture Ye on the Five Classics.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent the scholar Liu Huan to lecture Ye on the Five Classics in his commandery.

sentences.zh: 世祖即位，進號左將軍，入為中書令，將軍如故。

translations.literal: When the Shizu took the throne Ye was advanced to General of the Left and entered as director of the secretariat, general as before.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu ascended Ye was advanced to General of the Left and entered as director of the secretariat, rank unchanged.

sentences.zh: 轉散騎常侍，太常卿。

translations.literal: He was transferred attendant at leisure and grand minister of rituals.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to attendant at leisure and grand minister of rituals.

sentences.zh: 又 為中書令，遷祠部尚書，常侍並如故。

translations.literal: He was again director of the secretariat and promoted minister of imperial sacrifices, attendant as before.
translations.idiomatic: He was again director of the secretariat and promoted minister of imperial sacrifices, still attendant.

sentences.zh: 曄無寵於世祖，未嘗處方岳，數以語言忤旨。

translations.literal: Ye had no favor with the Shizu, never held a provincial post, and often offended by his words.
translations.idiomatic: Ye lacked Emperor Wu's favor, never held a provincial command, and often offended by his speech.

sentences.zh: 世祖幸豫章王嶷東田宴諸王，獨不召曄。

translations.literal: The Shizu visited Prince of Yuzhang Ni's eastern estate to feast the princes and alone did not summon Ye.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu feasted the princes at Prince of Yuzhang Ni's eastern estate and alone did not summon Ye.

sentences.zh: 嶷曰：「風景殊美，今日甚憶武陵。

translations.literal: Ni said: 「The scene is especially fine — today I greatly miss Wuling.」
translations.idiomatic: Ni said: 「The view is especially fine — today I sorely miss Wuling.」

sentences.zh: 」上乃呼之。

translations.literal: The emperor then called for him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then had him summoned.

sentences.zh: 曄善射，屢發命中，顧謂四坐曰：「手如何？

translations.literal: Ye was skilled at archery; shot after shot hit; he turned to the seated company and said: 「How is my hand?」
translations.idiomatic: Ye was a fine archer; shot after shot struck; he turned to the guests and said: 「How is my hand?」

sentences.zh: 」上神色甚怪。

translations.literal: The emperor's expression was very strange.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's expression turned very strange.

sentences.zh: 嶷曰：「阿五常日不爾，今可謂仰藉天威。

translations.literal: Ni said: 「Brother Five is not usually like this — today one may say he borrows Heaven's might.」
translations.idiomatic: Ni said: 「Brother Five is not usually so skilled — today he may be said to borrow Heaven's awesomeness.」

sentences.zh: 」帝意乃釋。

translations.literal: The emperor's mood then eased.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's mood then eased.

sentences.zh: 後於華林賭射，上敕曄疊破，凡放六箭，五破一皮，賜錢五萬。

translations.literal: Later at a Flowery Grove archery match the emperor ordered Ye to shoot in succession; of six arrows he broke five hides with one shot remaining and was granted fifty thousand cash.
translations.idiomatic: Later at Flowery Grove archery games the emperor ordered Ye to shoot in succession; of six arrows five broke the hide and one remained — he was granted fifty thousand cash.

sentences.zh: 又于御席上舉酒勸曄，曄曰：「陛下嘗不以此處許臣。

translations.literal: Again at the imperial mat he raised wine to urge Ye; Ye said: 「Your Majesty once did not grant me this place.」
translations.idiomatic: Again at the imperial feast he raised wine to toast Ye; Ye said: 「Your Majesty once would not grant me this seat.」

sentences.zh: 」上回面不答。

translations.literal: The emperor turned his face and did not answer.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor turned away and did not answer.

sentences.zh: 久之，出為江州刺史，常侍如故。

translations.literal: After long while he went out as governor of Jiang, attendant as before.
translations.idiomatic: After a long interval he went out as governor of Jiang, attendant as before.

sentences.zh: 上以曄方出外鎮，求曄宅給諸皇子。

translations.literal: Because Ye was about to go out to a frontier command, the emperor sought Ye's mansion to give the other princes.
translations.idiomatic: As Ye was leaving for an outer command, the emperor sought Ye's mansion to give to the other princes.

sentences.zh: 曄曰：「先帝賜臣此宅，使臣歌哭有所。

translations.literal: Ye said: 「The late emperor granted your servant this house, that your servant might have where to sing and weep.」
translations.idiomatic: Ye said: 「The late emperor gave me this house so I would have where to grieve and rejoice.」

sentences.zh: 陛下欲以州易宅，臣請不以宅易州。

translations.literal: 「If Your Majesty wishes to trade a province for the house, your servant asks not to trade the house for a province.」
translations.idiomatic: 「If Your Majesty wishes to trade a province for the house, I ask not to trade the house for a province.」

sentences.zh: 」至鎮百 餘日，典簽趙渥之啟曄得失，於是征還為左民尚書。

translations.literal: After he reached his post a little over a hundred days, chief clerk Zhao Wozhi memorialized Ye's faults and merits; he was recalled and made minister of the left for the people.
translations.idiomatic: After little more than a hundred days at post, chief clerk Zhao Wozhi reported Ye's faults and merits; he was recalled as minister of the left for the people.

sentences.zh: 俄轉前將軍，太常卿，累不得志。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred former general and grand minister of rituals, repeatedly thwarted in his aims.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was former general and grand minister of rituals, repeatedly thwarted.

sentences.zh: 冬節問訊，諸王皆出，曄獨後來，上已還便殿，聞曄至，引見問之。

translations.literal: At the winter solstice audience all princes went out; Ye alone came late; the emperor had already returned to the side hall; hearing Ye had arrived, he summoned and questioned him.
translations.idiomatic: At the winter solstice audience all princes departed; Ye alone came late; the emperor had returned to the side hall; hearing Ye had come, he summoned and questioned him.

sentences.zh: 曄稱 牛羸，不能取路。

translations.literal: Ye said his ox was exhausted and could not keep to the road.
translations.idiomatic: Ye said his ox was worn out and could not keep pace on the road.

sentences.zh: 上敕車府給副御牛一頭。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered the carriage office to give one extra imperial ox.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered the carriage office to supply one spare imperial ox.

sentences.zh: 敕主客：「自今諸王來不隨例者，不得復為通。」

translations.literal: He edicted the chief of guests: 「From now on princes who do not follow precedent shall not again be admitted.」
translations.idiomatic: He edicted the chief of guests: 「Hereafter princes who do not follow precedent shall not be admitted.」

sentences.zh: 以公事還過竟陵王子良宅，冬月道逢乞人，脫襦與之。

translations.literal: Returning on public business he passed Prince of Jingling Ziliang's residence; in winter on the road he met a beggar, took off his jacket and gave it.
translations.idiomatic: Returning on state business he passed Prince of Jingling Ziliang's house; in winter he met a beggar on the road, stripped off his jacket, and gave it.

sentences.zh: 子良見曄衣單，薦襦 于曄。

translations.literal: Ziliang saw Ye's clothes were thin and offered a jacket to Ye.
translations.idiomatic: Ziliang saw Ye was thinly clad and offered him a jacket.

sentences.zh: 曄曰：「我與向人亦復何異！

translations.literal: Ye said: 「What difference is there between me and the man just now!」
translations.idiomatic: Ye said: 「How am I different from the man I just met!」

sentences.zh: 」尚書令王儉詣曄，曄留儉設食，柈中菘 菜<魚邑>魚而已。

translations.literal: Director of the Secretariat Wang Jian visited Ye; Ye kept Jian and set out food — in the trays only turnip greens and pickled fish.
translations.idiomatic: Director Wang Jian visited Ye; Ye kept him to eat — the trays held only turnip greens and pickled fish.

sentences.zh: 又名後堂山為「首陽」，蓋怨貧薄也。

translations.literal: He also named the rear-hall mountain 「Shouyang,」 in resentment of poverty.
translations.idiomatic: He also named his rear-hall hill 「Shouyang,」 in mockery of his poverty.

sentences.zh: 尋為丹陽尹，常侍、將軍如故。

translations.literal: Soon he was governor of Danyang, attendant and general as before.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was governor of Danyang, attendant and general unchanged.

sentences.zh: 始不復置行事，得自親政。

translations.literal: For the first time he no longer had a acting staff but governed in person.
translations.idiomatic: For the first time he dispensed with a acting staff and governed in person.

sentences.zh: 轉侍中，護軍將 軍。

translations.literal: He was transferred attendant and Defender General.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred attendant and Defender General.

sentences.zh: 給油絡車。

translations.literal: He was given an oiled carriage canopy.
translations.idiomatic: He was given an oiled carriage canopy.

sentences.zh: 又給扶二人。

translations.literal: He was also given two men to support him.
translations.idiomatic: He was also given two attendants to support him.

sentences.zh: 世祖臨崩，遺詔為衛將軍，開府儀同三司，給鼓吹 一部。

translations.literal: As the Shizu lay near death, his final edict made Ye Defender General and Grand Mentor with Three-Dukes ceremony, with one set of martial pipes and drums.
translations.idiomatic: On his deathbed the Shizu's final edict made Ye Defender General and Grand Mentor with Three-Dukes ceremony, with martial pipes and drums.

sentences.zh: 大行在殯，竟陵王子良在殿內，太孫未立，眾論喧疑。

translations.literal: While the late emperor lay in coffin, Prince of Jingling Ziliang was in the hall; the heir apparent was not yet established — public talk was noisy with doubt.
translations.idiomatic: While the late emperor lay in state, Prince of Jingling Ziliang was in the hall and the heir was not yet named — rumor swirled.

sentences.zh: 曄眾中言曰：「若立 長則應在我，立嫡則應在太孫。

translations.literal: Ye said in the crowd: 「If the elder is to be enthroned it should be me; if the direct heir, it should be the heir apparent.」
translations.idiomatic: Ye said before the assembly: 「If the elder line is chosen it should be me; if the direct heir, it should be the crown prince.」

sentences.zh: 」郁林即立，甚見憑賴。

translations.literal: Emperor of Yulin was enthroned and Ye was greatly relied upon.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yulin was enthroned and Ye was greatly relied upon.

sentences.zh: 隆昌元年，年二十八， 薨。

translations.literal: In the first year of Longchang, aged twenty-eight, he died.
translations.idiomatic: In Longchang year one he died at twenty-eight.

sentences.zh: 賜東園秘器，朝服。

translations.literal: He was granted eastern-garden secret vessels and court dress.
translations.idiomatic: He was granted eastern-garden funeral regalia and court dress.

sentences.zh: 贈司空，侍中如故。

translations.literal: Posthumously made Minister of Works, attendant as before.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made Minister of Works, attendant as before.

sentences.zh: 給節，班劍二十人。

translations.literal: Credentials were granted and twenty guards with ceremonial swords.
translations.idiomatic: Credentials were granted and twenty guards with ceremonial swords.

sentences.zh: 延興元年，進位司徒，侍中、驃騎如故。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yanxing he was posthumously advanced to Grand Mentor, attendant and Rapid Cavalry as before.
translations.idiomatic: In Yanxing year one he was posthumously advanced to Grand Mentor, attendant and Rapid Cavalry unchanged.

sentences.zh: 高宗鎮東府，權勢稍異，鏘每往，高宗常屣履至車迎鏘。

translations.literal: When the High Emperor garrisoned the eastern mansion his power gradually differed; whenever Qiang came, the High Emperor often ran out in slippers to the carriage to welcome Qiang.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Ming garrisoned the eastern mansion his power grew distinct; whenever Qiang visited, Ming often ran out in slippers to his carriage to welcome him.

sentences.zh: 語及家國，言淚俱下，鏘以此推信之。

translations.literal: Speaking of state and family, words and tears together fell; Qiang therefore trusted him.
translations.idiomatic: Speaking of state and family they wept together; Qiang therefore trusted him.

sentences.zh: 而宮台內皆屬意於鏘，勸鏘入宮發兵輔政。

translations.literal: Within the palace all looked to Qiang and urged him to enter the palace and raise troops to assist government.
translations.idiomatic: Within the palace all looked to Qiang and urged him to enter, raise troops, and assist the government.

sentences.zh: 制局監謝粲說鏘及隨王子隆曰：「殿下但乘油壁車入宮，出天子置朝堂，二王夾輔號令，粲等閉城門上仗，誰敢不同？

translations.literal: Bureau supervisor Xie Can said to Qiang and Prince of Suizhou Zilong: 「Your Highness need only ride the oiled carriage into the palace, set the Son of Heaven in the court, the two princes flanking orders — Can and the rest shut the gates and arm the guard — who would not follow?
translations.idiomatic: Bureau supervisor Xie Can said to Qiang and Prince of Suizhou Zilong: 「Your Highness need only ride the lacquered carriage into the palace, set the Son of Heaven in court with two princes flanking command — we shut the gates and arm the guard — who would not follow?

sentences.zh: 東城人政共縛送蕭 令耳。

translations.literal: The eastern-city men would only bind and deliver the Xiao chief.」
translations.idiomatic: The eastern-city men would only bind and deliver Chief Xiao.」

sentences.zh: 」子隆欲定計，鏘以上台兵力既悉度東府，且慮事難捷，意甚猶豫。

translations.literal: Zilong wished to settle the plan; Qiang, because the upper court's military strength had all been shifted to the eastern mansion and he feared the affair would not be quick, was very hesitant.
translations.idiomatic: Zilong wished to fix the plan; Qiang, seeing court forces had all shifted to the eastern mansion and fearing the coup would not be swift, hesitated deeply.

sentences.zh: 馬隊主劉巨，世祖時舊人，詣鏘請間，叩頭勸鏘立事。

translations.literal: Horse-corps chief Liu Ju, an old man of the Shizu's time, visited Qiang privately, kowtowed and urged Qiang to act.
translations.idiomatic: Horse-corps chief Liu Ju, a veteran of Emperor Wu's day, visited Qiang in private, kowtowed, and urged him to act.

sentences.zh: 鏘命駕將入，復回還內與母陸 太妃別，日暮不成行。

translations.literal: Qiang ordered his carriage to enter, then turned back inside to part from his mother Consort Dowager Lu; by dusk he had not gone.
translations.idiomatic: Qiang ordered his carriage to enter, then turned back to farewell his mother, Consort Dowager Lu; by dusk he still had not gone.

sentences.zh: 數日，高宗遣二千人圍鏘宅害鏘，謝粲等皆見殺。

translations.literal: Several days later the High Emperor sent two thousand men to surround Qiang's mansion and kill him; Xie Can and the rest were all killed.
translations.idiomatic: Days later Emperor Ming sent two thousand men to surround Qiang's house and kill him; Xie Can and the rest were all slain.

sentences.zh: 鏘時年二十六。

translations.literal: Qiang was then twenty-six.
translations.idiomatic: Qiang was twenty-six.

sentences.zh: 凡諸王被害，皆以夜遣兵圍宅，或斧關排牆叫噪而入，家財皆見封籍焉。

translations.literal: Whenever princes were killed, troops were always sent at night to surround the mansion, or axes broke the gate and walls while shouting as they entered; family property was all sealed and inventoried.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever princes were killed, troops came by night to surround the house, or broke gates and walls with axes, shouting as they entered; household goods were all sealed and inventoried.

sentences.zh: 桂陽王鑠，字宣朗，太祖第八子也。

translations.literal: Prince of Guiyang Shuo, styled Xuanlang, was the founding emperor's eighth son.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Guiyang, Shuo, styled Xuanlang, was the founding emperor's eighth son.

sentences.zh: 永明二年，出為南徐州刺史，鎮京口。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yongming he went out as governor of Southern Xu, garrisoning Jingkou.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongming year two he went out as governor of Southern Xu, garrisoning Jingkou.

sentences.zh: 歷代鎮府，鑠出蕃，始省軍府。

translations.literal: Through the generations the garrison mansion had a military staff; when Shuo went out to his fief the staff was first abolished.
translations.idiomatic: For generations the garrison had kept a military staff; when Shuo took his fief the staff was abolished for the first time.

sentences.zh: 四年，加散騎常侍。

translations.literal: In year four he was made attendant at leisure.
translations.idiomatic: In year four he was made attendant at leisure.

sentences.zh: 六年，遷中書令，度支尚書。

translations.literal: In year six he was moved director of the secretariat and minister of revenue.
translations.idiomatic: In year six he was made director of the secretariat and minister of revenue.

sentences.zh: 七年，轉中書令，加散騎常侍。

translations.literal: In year seven he was again director of the secretariat with added attendant at leisure.
translations.idiomatic: In year seven he was again director of the secretariat with added attendant at leisure.

sentences.zh: 時鄱陽王鏘好文章，鑠好名理，時人稱為「鄱桂。

translations.literal: At the time Prince of Poyang Qiang loved literature and Shuo loved name-principles; contemporaries called them 「Poyang-Guiyang.」
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Poyang Qiang loved literature and Shuo loved abstruse principles; people called them 「Poyang and Guiyang.」

sentences.zh: 」十年，遷太常，常侍如故。

translations.literal: In year ten he was moved grand minister of rituals, attendant as before.
translations.idiomatic: In year ten he was moved to grand minister of rituals, attendant unchanged.

sentences.zh: 鑠清羸有冷疾，常枕臥。

translations.literal: Shuo was slight and frail with a cold ailment and often lay on a pillow.
translations.idiomatic: Shuo was slight and frail with a chill disorder and often lay abed.

sentences.zh: 世祖臨視，賜床帳衾褥。

translations.literal: The Shizu visited him in person and granted bed curtains and coverlets.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu visited him in person and granted bedding and coverlets.

sentences.zh: 隆 昌元年，加前將軍。

translations.literal: In the first year of Longchang he was made former general.
translations.idiomatic: In Longchang year one he was made former general.

sentences.zh: 給油絡車，並給扶侍二人。

translations.literal: He was given an oiled carriage canopy and two attendants to support him.
translations.idiomatic: He was given an oiled carriage canopy and two supporting attendants.

sentences.zh: 海陵立，轉侍中、撫軍將軍，領兵置佐。

translations.literal: When Emperor of Hailing was enthroned he was transferred attendant and Pacification General with military staff appointed.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Hailing ascended he was attendant and Pacification General with military staff.

sentences.zh: 鄱陽王見害，鑠遷中軍將軍，開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: When Prince of Poyang was killed, Shuo was moved general of the central army and Grand Mentor with Three-Dukes ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Poyang was killed, Shuo was made general of the central army and Grand Mentor with Three-Dukes ceremony.

sentences.zh: 鑠不自安，至東府詣高宗還， 謂左右曰：「向錄公見接殷勤，流連不能已，而貌有慚色，此必欲殺我。

translations.literal: Shuo was ill at ease; returning from visiting the High Emperor at the eastern mansion he said to his attendants: 「The Chief Recorder received me with such eager kindness I could not leave, yet his face had a guilty look — he must intend to kill me.」
translations.idiomatic: Shuo was uneasy; returning from visiting Emperor Ming at the eastern mansion he told his attendants: 「The Chief Recorder received me so warmly I could not tear myself away, yet his face showed shame — he must mean to kill me.」

sentences.zh: 」三更 中，兵至見害。

translations.literal: In the third watch troops arrived and he was killed.
translations.idiomatic: In the third watch troops came and killed him.

sentences.zh: 時年二十五。

translations.literal: He was then twenty-five.
translations.idiomatic: He was twenty-five.

sentences.zh: 始興簡王鑒，字宣徹，太祖第十子也。

translations.literal: Prince Jian of Shixing, styled Xuanche, was the founding emperor's tenth son.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Jian of Shixing, Jian, styled Xuanche, was the founding emperor's tenth son.

sentences.zh: 初封廣興王，后國隨郡改名。

translations.literal: He was first enfeoffed Prince of Guangxing; later the state followed Suizhou and the name was changed.
translations.idiomatic: He was first enfeoffed Prince of Guangxing; later the fief moved to Suizhou and the title changed.

sentences.zh: 永明二年，世祖始以鑒為持節、都督益寧二州軍事、前將軍、益州刺史。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yongming the Shizu first made Jian bearer of credentials, commander of Yi and Ning, former general, and governor of Yi.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongming year two Emperor Wu first made Jian bearer of credentials, commander of Yi and Ning, former general, and governor of Yi.

sentences.zh: 廣漢什邡民段 祖以錞于獻鑒，古禮器也。

translations.literal: Duan Zu of Shifang in Guanghan presented Jian with a chunyu — an ancient ritual vessel.
translations.idiomatic: Duan Zu of Shifang in Guanghan presented Jian with a chunyu — an ancient ritual bell.

sentences.zh: 高三尺六寸六分，圍二尺四寸，圓如筒，銅色黑如漆，甚薄。

translations.literal: It was three chi six cun six fen high, circumference two chi four cun, round like a tube, copper colored black as lacquer, very thin.
translations.idiomatic: It stood three chi six cun six fen high, two chi four cun around, round as a tube, copper black as lacquer, very thin.

sentences.zh: 上有銅馬，以繩縣馬，令去地尺餘，灌之以水，又以器盛水于下，以 芒莖當心跪注錞于，以手振芒，則其聲如雷，清響良久乃絕。

translations.literal: Above was a bronze horse; a rope suspended the horse a little over a chi from the ground; water was poured in, and a vessel of water placed below; with a rush stem at the center kneeling to pour into the chunyu, shaking the rush by hand, the sound was like thunder, clear and long before it ceased.
translations.idiomatic: A bronze horse hung above; rope held it a foot from the ground; water was poured in and a basin set below; kneeling, one poured through a rush at the center — shake the rush and the tone rolled like thunder, clear and long before fading.

sentences.zh: 古所以節樂也。

translations.literal: In antiquity it was thus that music was regulated.
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity music was regulated thus.

sentences.zh: 五年，鑒獻龍角一枚，長九尺三寸，色紅，有文。

translations.literal: In year five Jian presented one dragon horn, nine chi three cun long, red with markings.
translations.idiomatic: In year five Jian presented a dragon horn nine chi three cun long, red and patterned.

sentences.zh: 八年，進號安西將軍。

translations.literal: In year eight he was advanced General Who Pacifies the West.
translations.idiomatic: In year eight he was advanced to General Who Pacifies the West.

sentences.zh: 鋒好琴書，有武力。

translations.literal: Feng loved zither and books and had martial strength.
translations.idiomatic: Feng loved zither and books and possessed martial strength.

sentences.zh: 高宗殺諸王，鋒遺書誚責，左右不為通，高宗深憚之。

translations.literal: When the High Emperor killed the princes, Feng sent a letter of rebuke; his attendants did not pass it through — the High Emperor deeply feared him.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Ming slaughtered the princes, Feng sent a letter of rebuke; attendants would not deliver it — Ming feared him deeply.

sentences.zh: 不敢於第收鋒，使兼祠官于太廟，夜遣兵廟中收之。

translations.literal: He dared not seize Feng at his mansion and made him an acting sacrifices officer at the imperial temple, sending troops at night to seize him in the temple.
translations.idiomatic: He dared not take Feng at his house and made him acting temple sacrifices officer, then sent troops at night to seize him in the temple.

sentences.zh: 鋒出登車，兵人慾上車防勒， 鋒以手擊卻數人，皆應時倒地，於是敢近者遂逼害之。

translations.literal: Feng came out and mounted the carriage; soldiers wished to board and restrain him — Feng with his hands struck down several men, all falling at once; none dared approach, and they forced and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Feng came out and mounted his carriage; soldiers tried to board and seize him — Feng struck down several with his hands, each falling at once; none dared near, and they pressed in and killed him.

sentences.zh: 時年二十。

translations.literal: He was then twenty.
translations.idiomatic: He was twenty.

sentences.zh: 南平王銳，字宣毅，太祖第十五子也。

translations.literal: Prince of Nanping Rui, styled Xuanyi, was the founding emperor's fifteenth son.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Nanping, Rui, styled Xuanyi, was the founding emperor's fifteenth son.

sentences.zh: 永明七年，為散騎常侍，尋領驍騎將軍。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Yongming he was attendant at leisure, soon head of the Valiant Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongming year seven he was attendant at leisure, soon head of the Valiant Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 明年，為左民尚書。

translations.literal: The next year he was minister of the left for the people.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he was minister of the left for the people.

sentences.zh: 朝直勤謹，未嘗屬疾，上嘉之。

translations.literal: At court he was diligent and never claimed illness; the emperor praised him.
translations.idiomatic: At court he was diligent and never pleaded illness; the emperor praised him.

sentences.zh: 十年，出為持節、都督 湘州諸軍事、南中郎將、湘州刺史，以此賞銳。

translations.literal: In year ten he went out bearer of credentials, commander of Xiang, General of the South Center, and governor of Xiang — for this he was rewarded.
translations.idiomatic: In year ten he went out bearer of credentials, commander of Xiang, General of the South Center, and governor of Xiang — in reward for his service.

sentences.zh: 郁林即位，進號前將軍。

translations.literal: When Emperor of Yulin took the throne he was advanced former general.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yulin ascended he was advanced to former general.

sentences.zh: 延興元年，害諸王，遣裴叔業平尋陽，仍進湘州。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yanxing, when the princes were killed, Pei Shuye was sent to pacify Xunyang and then advanced into Xiang.
translations.idiomatic: In Yanxing year one, when the princes were killed, Pei Shuye pacified Xunyang and advanced into Xiang.

sentences.zh: 銳防閣周伯玉勸銳拒叔業， 而府州力弱不敢動，銳見害，年十九。

translations.literal: Rui's guard-chamberlain Zhou Boyu urged Rui to resist Shuye, but the princedom and prefecture were too weak to move; Rui was killed, aged nineteen.
translations.idiomatic: Rui's guard-chamberlain Zhou Boyu urged resistance to Shuye, but princedom and prefecture were too weak; Rui was killed at nineteen.

sentences.zh: 伯玉下獄誅。

translations.literal: Boyu was imprisoned and executed.
translations.idiomatic: Boyu was imprisoned and executed.

sentences.zh: 河東王鉉，字宣胤，太祖第十九子也。

translations.literal: Prince of Hedong Xuan, styled Xuanyi, was the founding emperor's nineteenth son.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Hedong, Xuan, styled Xuanyi, was the founding emperor's nineteenth son.

sentences.zh: 隆昌元年，為驍騎將軍。

translations.literal: In the first year of Longchang he was head of the Valiant Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: In Longchang year one he was head of the Valiant Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 出為徐州刺 史，遷中書令。

translations.literal: He went out governor of Xu, then was moved director of the secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He went out as governor of Xu, then was moved director of the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 高宗誅諸王，以鉉年少才弱，故不加害。

translations.literal: When the High Emperor executed the princes, because Xuan was young and weak in talent he was not harmed.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Ming executed the princes, Xuan was young and slight in ability and was spared.

sentences.zh: 建武元年，轉為散騎常 侍，鎮軍將軍，置兵佐。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jianwu he was transferred attendant at leisure and General Who Guards the Army with military staff.
translations.idiomatic: In Jianwu year one he was attendant at leisure and General Who Guards the Army with military staff.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：陳思王表云：「權之所存，雖疏必重；

translations.literal: The historian says: In Prince Si of Chen's memorial it states: 「Where power resides, though distant one must honor it;
translations.idiomatic: The historian says: Prince Si of Chen's memorial states: 「Where power resides, though distant one must honor it;

sentences.zh: 勢之所去，雖親必輕。

translations.literal: where influence departs, though near one must treat lightly.」
translations.idiomatic: where influence departs, though near one must treat it lightly.」

sentences.zh: 」若夫六代之興亡，曹冏論之當矣。

translations.literal: As for the rise and fall of the six ages, Cao Tong's discussion is apt.
translations.idiomatic: On the rise and fall of the six dynasties, Cao Tong's argument is apt.

sentences.zh: 分圭命社，實寄宗城。

translations.literal: Granting halves of jade and ordering altars of earth truly entrusts the walled cities.
translations.idiomatic: Granting jade halves and ordering earth altars truly entrust the royal cities.

sentences.zh: 就國之典，既隨世革，卿 士入朝，作貴蕃輔。

translations.literal: The institution of going to one's state changed with the age; ministers and grandees entering court became honored frontier assistants.
translations.idiomatic: The institution of taking up a fief changed with the times; ministers entering court became honored assistants in the regions.

sentences.zh: 皇王托體，同稟尊極，仕無常資，秩有恆數，禮地兼隆，易生猜疑。

translations.literal: Imperial princes in body share the utmost honor; office has no fixed salary, rank has constant numbers — ritual and territory alike exalted, suspicion easily arises.
translations.idiomatic: Princes in body share supreme honor; office has no fixed stipend, rank has set numbers — ritual and territory both lofty, and suspicion comes easily.

sentences.zh: 世祖顧命，情深尊嫡，淵圖遠算，意在無遺。

translations.literal: The Shizu's final charge was deep in honoring the direct heir; his far-reaching design intended no omission.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu's deathbed charge deeply honored the direct heir; his far-reaching design intended to leave nothing out.

sentences.zh: 豈不以群王少弱，未更多 難，高宗清謹，同起布衣，故韜末命于近親，寄重權于疏戚，子弟布列，外有強大之勢，疏親中立，可息覬覦之謀，表裡相維，足固家國。

translations.literal: Was it not because the princes were young and weak, with no further troubles yet, and the High Emperor was careful and pure, rising together from coarse cloth, that he tucked the last command among close kin and entrusted heavy power to distant kin — younger brothers arrayed outside with strong force, distant and close balanced within to quiet covetous schemes, inner and outer mutually sustaining, enough to secure house and state?
translations.idiomatic: Was it not because the princes were young and untested, the High Emperor careful and upright, having risen from common cloth together, that he tucked his last words among close kin and lodged heavy power with distant kin — brothers deployed outside with strong force, distant and close balanced within to still greedy designs, inner and outer sustaining each other, enough to secure the house?

sentences.zh: 曾不慮機能運衡，權 可制眾，宗族殲滅，一至於斯。

translations.literal: He never considered that craft could turn the balance and power could control the multitude — the clan extinguished, all at once to this point.
translations.idiomatic: He never considered that craft could turn the scales and power control the masses — the clan annihilated, all at once to this end.

sentences.zh: 曹植之言信之矣。

translations.literal: Cao Zhi's words were proved true.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Zhi's words proved true.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：高十二王，始建封植。

translations.literal: Eulogy: The High Emperor's twelve princes first received enfeoffment and planting.
translations.idiomatic: Eulogy: The twelve princes of Emperor Gao first received fiefs and were planted in office.

sentences.zh: 獻、昭機警，威、江才力。

translations.literal: Xian and Zhao were sharp-witted; Wei and Jiang had talent and force.
translations.idiomatic: The Xian and Zhao princes were sharp-witted; the Wei and Jiang princes had talent and force.

sentences.zh: 恭、簡恬和，鄱、 桂清識。

translations.literal: Gong and Jian were mild and harmonious; Poyang and Guiyang had pure insight.
translations.idiomatic: The Gong and Jian princes were mild and harmonious; the Poyang and Guiyang princes had clear judgment.

sentences.zh: 四王少盛，同規謹敕。

translations.literal: The four younger princes in their prime shared one rule of careful discipline.
translations.idiomatic: Four younger princes in their prime shared one standard of careful restraint.
